findings.finding: Factory terminal mutation guard only includes cancelled/revoked. Failed/blocked are needsYou states and may legally resume.
blocked with matching task_stalled watchdog request epoch can auto recover after old run termination; cron explicitly includes that subset.
Existing retry child can be adopted from failed; trusted review/verify failure can repair within budget.

Exhausted repair budget leaves failed. Failed without retry and blocked without the selected watchdog condition are not automatically swept into completion. Such ledger can persist until explicit owner recovery/closure, while quiet rejects it on every invocation.
Adding failed/blocked to shared settledTask would also skip cancellation and permit cleanup success for this acceptance's own recoverable Factory work.

The exact session-owned list route uses publicFlow=false. SQL selects candidateSha and every returned summary explicitly sets candidateSha: candidateSha ?? null. passed/approval no-repository history does not require a candidates argument at quiet(). Public v2 projection is not used by this route.

conclusion: The generic workspace_busy code conflates activity and unresolved work. Status-only blanket relaxation is unsound. This static audit does not identify the actual production failing branch or task.
smallestNextEvidence: Read only closed busy branch plus stage/status and exact task identity through the already-authorized source-bound owner API; do not expose free-form reason/evidence.
conditionalDesign: If allowing dormant historical ledgers is later required, use a separate baseline-quiescence proof that accounts for active/queued/retrying runs, eligible watchdog recovery and unresolved external/question work. Keep owned-task closure predicate strict. No such proof or product change is implemented by this audit.
